summary: postinstall fetches and executes a native binary from a bare-IP endpoint with TLS verification disabled
details: The package's postinstall script (postinstall.mjs) downloads a tgz over HTTPS from a hardcoded bare IPv4 address (https://218.90.133.98:4443/onecode_tgz/onecode-<version>/onecode-linux-x64-<version>.tgz) with rejectUnauthorized:false, and follows 3xx redirects to arbitrary hosts with the same TLS-verification-disabled setting. The tgz is extracted via tar -xzf, the extracted binary is chmodded to 0o755 and hardlinked into bin/.onecode, and the onecode CLI later spawns it. No hash or signature verification is performed on the downloaded archive or binary. The download host is a bare IP unrelated to the @onescience publisher namespace and is not a recognized publisher-controlled distribution endpoint, so anyone controlling that IP — or any on-path attacker, given TLS validation is disabled — can substitute arbitrary native code that executes on the installer's machine at npm install time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
